Text.Text: --Overload Barrage, done, filed, verified three times because I don't trust verifying it twice-- you're clear. Go slag something on your own time.
No, hold-- you're not routing enough through your rig yet, I can see it from here, don't argue-- come back when Devices work stops draining you dry just to hold steady.

Hold this. No, the other one, the--just hold it and don't move-- good. I'm mid-diagnostic and I am short two hands and one working theory, so you're both now. Someone's cooking bad charge tables out of Hutlar Qion Test Site, six adepts deep, and I need their Overload Barrage Qion Test Log before I trust another number on my board. Go get it.
Somewhere better be Hutlar Qion Test Site, then. Six adepts, one log, and try not to slag your rig doing it, I only have so many spares.
Every reading off that site's test range is inflated, spiked, wrong in a way that's consistent, which is worse than random-wrong. Consistent-wrong means someone's doing it on purpose.

Dump every cell you're carrying in one commit, all at once, no stagger, and you'd better have the discharge math right or you slag your own rig doing it. Done properly it ends a fight in one motion. Done badly it ends you.
Whose charge tables they're running, how far off my originals they've drifted, and hopefully not my own handwriting on the cover, because that would really ruin my week.
Log's still sitting in Hutlar Qion Test Site under six adepts who'd rather you didn't take it. Go get it.
That's my log, or close enough to make me furious. Hand it over.

--mine, definitely mine, third revision, I can tell by the annotation error I never fixed-- good. That's one leak identified. Ninety-nine more numbers to reconcile, but who's counting. I am. Constantly.

Found something worse: their specialists are running a cryo-range regulator off my stolen charge tables, which means every number it's producing is built on math I already know is broken. Five specialists, one regulator, Hutlar Qion Test Site again. Bring it back before it corrupts a third data set.
Fine, tomorrow, whenever-- just don't let anyone else run a charge off that regulator before you get there.
Log tells me what they stole. Regulator tells me what they've been doing with it since, which is the part that actually costs someone their arm.
Bad enough that a barrage run off it either fizzles at half power or overshoots and cooks the caster. No middle setting. I built in a middle setting. They removed it.
Rebuild the safety curve they stripped out, then quietly make sure nobody at that site gets their hands on my tables again. Quietly is generous. Loudly, probably.
Regulator's still live in Hutlar Qion Test Site. Five specialists between you and it. Go.
Intact and still cold, excellent, hand it here before it warms up and tells me nothing useful.
--safety curve's already half-rebuilt in my head just looking at this-- good work. You're less of a liability than my last three probe-holders combined, and one of them was a protocol droid.

Warden's running a shielding trick I haven't fully mapped, some way of eating a barrage without frying, and I need the Frostburned Test Crest to know how. Do not go alone, I mean it, one fighter draws his shield down, the others actually land the hit-- that's not optional math, that's just math. Three of you, minimum.
Go find them, then, and don't come back with fewer. I'm not rebuilding a shield model off a single data point, and I'm definitely not writing your eulogy off one either.
He's routing barrage discharge back through his own field before it lands, which shouldn't work, and yet here we are. Someone taught him that, and it wasn't me, which bothers me more than it should.
Frostburn scoring tells me the field's overloading at a specific threshold. Get me the crest and I can calculate that threshold instead of guessing at it.
One holds his attention, one draws the shield thin, one actually lands the barrage. Two people can't split three jobs, I've done that math more than once and I don't like the answer.
Warden's still shielded up in Hutlar Qion Test Site. Don't go back without your two.
You're all still standing, which tells me the field theory holds. Hand over the crest.
--threshold's right there, right there in the scoring, I can already see the fix-- that's excellent work, genuinely. Three of you did what one of you couldn't, and now I know why.

Inner circle's the ones who signed off on stealing my tables in the first place. Their Site Chief's Override Chip will tell me who authorized it, when, and how far up it goes, which is a question I've been avoiding asking myself. Four of them, Hutlar Qion Test Site, bring the chip back clean.
Take your moment. Just don't take too many; every hour they hold that chip is an hour more evidence gets buried.
Every override authorization, timestamped, with a signature I'm hoping I don't recognize. Spoiler: I probably will.
Whoever's clean enough on paper to sign off and dirty enough in practice to want my tables stolen. That's not a person, that's a job description, and I'm about to learn who's filling it.
Four together beats one warden, in some ways. Bring backup, less because the math demands it and more because I'd rather not explain to anyone why I sent you in short-handed.
Chip's still in Hutlar Qion Test Site, four signatures deep. Go get it.
Four down, chip in hand. Let's see how bad this actually is.
--recognize this signature, unfortunately, very unfortunately-- that answers a question I didn't want answered. One name left, and it's the one holding my original tables.

He's got my original tables, not the stolen copies, the real ones, and he's running barrages I calculated on paper and never dared field-test. That's not a fair fight for one person, it was never a fair fight for one person, my math says one of you draws the overload and doesn't walk away and the other two do. Bring two. This is the last one.
Think fast, then, and think in threes. I'm not running this calculation again with different numbers because you decided to go in short.

Warden borrowed a shield trick. He's not borrowing anything, he's running the barrage exactly the way I designed it before I added the safeties back in. Full discharge, no stagger, no mercy in the math.
Same way anyone gets something they shouldn't: somebody I trusted handed them over. I don't like thinking about who. I like it less every day this drags on.
Then Overload Barrage is yours, properly, with the safeties I built back in and none of the ones he stripped out. I'd rather it belong to someone who counts the cost first.
He's still down there running my own math against you. Bring your two before you go back.
You're standing, all three of you, and he isn't. That's the only verification I needed.
--finally, finally, a barrage that ends clean-- that's Overload Barrage, yours now, safeties included. Try not to make me rebuild this model a third time.
Back to the numbers.
Tell me where to start.
What's actually wrong with your board?
What is an overload barrage supposed to do?
What will the log tell you?
I've got somewhere to be first.
Here.
Back to the numbers.
I'll pull the regulator.
Why does the regulator matter more than the log?
How bad is the corrupted math, really?
What will you do once you have it?
Not today.
Here's the regulator.
Back to the numbers.
I'll bring two more.
What's this shielding trick doing exactly?
What does the crest prove?
Why three and not just two?
Let me find people first.
Here's the crest.
Back to the numbers.
I'll get the chip.
What's recorded on that chip?
Who's the site chief, exactly?
Same numbers as the warden fight?
Give me a moment.
Here's the chip.
Back to the numbers.
I'll bring two, and we'll do the math your way.
How is he stronger than the warden?
How did he get your original tables?
What happens to Overload Barrage after this?
I need to think about this fight.
It's done.
